title: Credibility assessment of implicit finite element models for coronary stent fatigue and radial strength under a risk-based V&V framework

models.name: Model U (Unit-cell implicit FEA)
models.what_it_computes: Periodic strut–connector unit-cell simulation to compute stabilized cyclic equivalent strain/stress amplitudes, mean stress, and local fatigue safety factors under representative in vivo load cycles.

models.name: Model S (System-level implicit FEA)
models.what_it_computes: Full stent model through crimp–expand–release with residual stress carryover, followed by quasi-static radial compression and physiologic pulsatile loading to compute radial strength, recoil, global stress distribution, and hotspot identification.

mechanisms.name: Pulsatile fatigue of struts and connectors
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Crack initiation and fracture can lead to loss of scaffolding, restenosis, or thrombosis; accurate stress/strain cycling is essential for durability predictions.

mechanisms.name: Radial crush strength
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Resistance to external compression preserves lumen patency and supports vessel walls during acute and chronic loading.

mechanisms.name: Crimp/expansion plasticity and residual stress
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Manufacturing and deployment plastic strains set the initial damage state, influence fatigue margins, and affect post-deployment stiffness and recoil.

clear_factors: Relevance of the validation activities to the COU

deviation.detail: Credibility Attainment Score (CAS) reported on a 0–5 numeric scale per factor for each model–mechanism pair, with predefined acceptability thresholds.

sections: Introduction: objective and scope limited to fatigue and radial strength credibility for an implicit FEA coronary stent program
Device and computational models: geometry, materials, boundary conditions, and solver settings for Model U and Model S

Context of Use (COU): Quantitative use of Models U and S to support design verification and regulatory submissions by (i) predicting fatigue safety factors at strut/connector hotspots under physiologic pulsatile loading and (ii) predicting minimum radial strength under quasi-static compression across a family of stent sizes; models guide design down-selection and set pre-test acceptance bands while bench tests per applicable standards remain the release gate; rationale: the models directly inform design decisions and acceptance criteria but are complemented by physical testing, and are not used for patient-specific clinical decisions

Model risk level and rationale: Risk categorized as Medium based on decision consequence (moderate—incorrect predictions could allow a suboptimal design to advance, yet bench testing and standards-based verification remain mandatory barriers) and model influence (moderate-to-high—the models bound design space, set acceptance bands, and may retire some bench iterations); combined as Medium with justification in terms of device function, potential clinical impact of structural failure, and multi-evidence decision process
Mechanisms and mapping of models to mechanisms: assignment of Model U and Model S to each of the three mechanisms; definition of outputs per mechanism
Credibility plan and acceptance criteria: factor-by-factor plan; CAS 0–5 thresholds for acceptability per mechanism and model; planned evidentiary artifacts and traceability matrix
Verification activities—Discretization error: mesh refinement, local error indicators at hotspots, and convergence of radial stiffness for each model–mechanism pair; reporting CAS per pair
Verification activities—Numerical solver error: nonlinear convergence tolerances, load/time stepping studies, contact stabilization evaluation; reporting CAS per pair
Verification activities—Numerical code verification: vendor code verification summary referenced and internal spot checks noted; brief rationale provided; CAS per pair presented

Model inputs: material model selection, plasticity and cyclic properties, crimp/expansion process parameters, boundary conditions, physiologic load spectra; input variability and traceability to sources; CAS per pair

Validation—Output comparison: bench radial compression tests, fatigue coupon/segment tests, and deployment strain imaging comparators mapped to model outputs; statistical agreement metrics and uncertainty treatment; CAS per pair
Validation—Relevance of the validation activities to the COU: justification that selected tests and comparators bound the intended COU operating envelope and decision variables; CAS per pair
Software quality assurance: configuration control, verification test suites, requirements traceability, and change management as applied to the modeling workflow; CAS per pair
Results: CAS scores matrix (2 models × 3 mechanisms × 7 factors) with per-cell rationale and acceptance status
Discussion: interpretation of factor-wise CAS, dominant contributors to uncertainty, and implications for design decisions within the stated COU
Limitations: scope restricted to specified mechanisms and factors; generalizability bounded by tested materials and sizes
Conclusions: credibility sufficiency within Medium risk COU; recommendations for sustaining evidence in future submissions
